question.text: Chapter 9 states SEBI (AIF) Regulations require VC investments to be made in companies offering __. Which description matches?

answer.text: Only listed securities and blue-chip equities.
New products, new services, technology or intellectual property-based activities or a new business model — nascent ventures with high growth potential.
Only real-estate developers in Tier-1 cities.

explanation.text: The Logic: Chapter 9 reproduces the SEBI (AIF) Regulations requirement that VC investments should be made in companies offering new products, new services, technology or intellectual property-based activities or a new business model. The workbook frames these as nascent ventures with high growth potential, which is the core VC mandate. The Trap: Option A contradicts the unlisted, early-stage character of VC investments. Options C and D invent restrictions (PSU stake sales or Tier-1 real estate) that have no basis in the SEBI VC definition. Note: Match every option against the four specific elements in the VC definition — new products, new services, technology or IP-based activities, or a new business model — before selecting.
